one_line: An agent-guided coding classroom embedded in a structured WebMCP learning workspace.
what_it_does: Teaches HTML, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript through lessons, code examples, explanations, exercises, and validation in one browser classroom.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP gives the tutor structured access to lesson state and coding-workspace actions, improving in-context guidance, but a general agent could reproduce much of the interaction with UI automation at some friction.
leverage_evidence: Devpost pitch explicitly describes safe, structured WebMCP tools.
Frames show an embedded guide explaining highlighted code and an interactive lesson workspace.
About text says the agent creates learning plans, examples, and exercises.
execution_rationale: The packet coherently shows a functioning-looking classroom, editor, lesson navigation, guide, and exercises, though no video is submitted and end-to-end completion evidence is limited.
execution_evidence: Three frame sheets show lesson UI, code editor, highlighted code, guide cards, and exercise states.
Devpost screenshot shows a connected WebMCP classroom and HTML exercise.
Live demo is reported alive.
impact_rationale: Beginning programmers have a clear need for contextual explanations and guided practice; the product directly addresses the gap between explanation and application.
impact_evidence: About text identifies novice HTML/CSS/JavaScript learners and frustration with disconnected guidance.
Frames visibly combine instruction, code, and practice.
creativity_rationale: An in-editor agent-led classroom with contextual highlighting and practice is a fresh synthesis beyond generic coding chat, though the educational category is established.
creativity_evidence: Agent explanations are attached to highlighted code inside the classroom.
The learner, rather than the agent, performs exercises.
usability_note: The visible guided layout is approachable, but the packet does not establish robustness across lessons or users.
red_flags: No submitted video; several capabilities are claimed rather than demonstrated end-to-end.
standouts: Clear human-learning role for the agent.
Strong visual coupling between explanation and code.
advance_reason: Strong educational fit and credible integrated classroom, with meaningful WebMCP value despite limited end-to-end evidence.

one_line: A human-controlled adaptive path that breaks overwhelming goals into accepted micro-steps.
what_it_does: Lets a person state a difficult goal, receive smaller proposals from an agent, accept or reject them, signal friction, and track or undo progress.
leverage_rationale: The agent and person share structured live goal, path, friction, progress, and undo state while preserving a deliberate approval boundary; this is materially safer and more reliable than pixel-driven automation.
leverage_evidence: About text specifies structured tools for get state, propose, accept, complete, and undo.
Frames show adaptive goal onboarding and CV micro-step flow.
Agent proposals cannot silently apply without UI acceptance.
execution_rationale: The visual packet shows a coherent onboarding and CV path with progress and adaptation, but lacks video and live end-to-end proof.
execution_evidence: Three frame sheets show goal prompt, one-clear-next-step flow, checklist, CV task, and progress states.
Devpost packaging states AI proposes and user decides.
Live demo is reported alive.
impact_rationale: People facing cognitively or emotionally overwhelming goals are a specific audience, and reducing the next action while retaining agency is a credible benefit.
impact_evidence: About text gives job-loss and CV completion as a concrete use case.
Frames show a calmer step-by-step workflow with friction adaptation.
creativity_rationale: The explicit friction signal and human-only acceptance boundary form a notably original interaction model for agent assistance.
creativity_evidence: User action 'This feels like too much' causes a smaller replacement proposal.
Visible undo and acceptance boundary are central, not decorative.
usability_note: The uncluttered one-step flow and visible progress support approachable use; robustness beyond the shown CV path is unverified.
red_flags: No submitted video; claims about live WebMCP interaction are primarily textual/packaging evidence.
advance_reason: Distinctive, high-value human-agent collaboration pattern with credible visual evidence.

one_line: A studio where agents author, direct, review, and export fictional coding-agent sessions.
what_it_does: Uses scripts, stage controls, camera, timeline inspection, approvals, snapshots, and export to create deterministic SVG/video demonstrations without exposing real session secrets.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP lets the agent operate on and inspect the live stage, timeline, frames, and approval state; a general UI-driving agent could not comparably reliably author and validate precise timed media.
leverage_evidence: 170-second video transcript reports tool registration, load_script, camera, timeline, snapshots, proposals, approvals, and export.
Frames show agent authoring, stage playback, choices, and changing rendered output.
About text says the agent works on the stage rather than a guess.
execution_rationale: The unusually complete transcript and frame sheets demonstrate a coherent author-to-playback-to-review-to-export workflow with human approvals.
execution_evidence: Video is present and 170 seconds long with detailed end-to-end transcript.
Frames show authoring panels, rendered stage, choice interaction, and playback states.
About text specifies deterministic SVG/CSS export and receipts.
impact_rationale: Documentation, talks, and posts need repeatable fictional agent-session visuals that avoid secret leakage and can be revised; the product directly serves that niche.
impact_evidence: About text identifies README, docs, talks, and posts as users.
Export and re-shootability are shown as core workflow goals.
creativity_rationale: The concept of an agent-directed, reviewable stage for deterministic fictional sessions is memorable and pursued deeply across scripting, interaction, camera, and export.
creativity_evidence: Agent writes scripts while the person approves rewrites and export.
Same script can render app and terminal surfaces with timed interactions.
usability_note: The staged workflow and approvals are clear; the breadth of 13 tools may increase complexity for new users.
advance_reason: Best-supported packet: WebMCP is central, workflow is demonstrated end-to-end, and the concept is distinctive.

one_line: A shared cloud architecture canvas where agents simulate STRIDE threats and patch the graph.
what_it_does: Lets humans sketch infrastructure, agents read topology, draw attacks, apply bounded mitigations, and report remaining security issues on the same live graph.
leverage_rationale: Structured graph state and typed mutations are important for precise security analysis and shared visual patching; screenshot automation would be unreliable for topology and mitigation state.
leverage_evidence: About text specifies get_architecture_state, simulate_attack, apply_security_patch, and get_threat_report.
Frames show a node-based workflow/canvas and configuration panels.
Devpost screenshot visibly shows architecture canvas, attacker node, WAF, and agent activity.
execution_rationale: The canvas and workflow are coherent and the demo packaging is specific, but there is no submitted video and the packet cannot verify the full attack-to-patch loop.
execution_evidence: Three frame sheets show an editable workflow/graph interface with node states.
About text gives a concrete insecure 3-tier starter and patch flow.
Live demo is reported alive.
impact_rationale: Small technical teams have a real need for inspectable early security design; the product addresses threat discovery and remediation in their working artifact.
impact_evidence: About text identifies security-by-design cloud architecture as the target niche.
Visible canvas includes architecture components and threat visualization.
creativity_rationale: Combining live spatial architecture editing with STRIDE simulation and agent-applied patches is a fresh, coherent interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Attacks are drawn directly onto the shared graph.
Mitigations are applied and verified in the activity log.
usability_note: The graph-centric workflow is legible for technical users, though complexity and correctness of threat modeling need deeper observation.
red_flags: No video; security correctness and complete mutation sequence are not independently demonstrated.
standouts: Auditable activity log and bounded patches.
advance_reason: High-value technical workflow where structured live graph access materially improves agent reliability.

one_line: A browser zk-SNARK workstation that proves genetic drug contraindications without sharing raw DNA.
what_it_does: Parses genetic data locally and produces zero-knowledge Groth16 proofs for pharmacogenomic conclusions exposed to an agent without revealing the underlying genome.
leverage_rationale: The privacy-preserving design changes what an agent can safely know: structured proof results replace impossible-to-share raw genetic context, making the agent interface materially different from UI automation.
leverage_evidence: Pitch and about text explicitly combine WebMCP with in-browser Groth16 proofs.
The stated workflow keeps raw DNA on device while exposing conclusions.
No video frames were submitted, so live tool operation is not visually verified.
execution_rationale: The concept and technical claims are coherent, but the packet has no video frames and the Devpost screenshot is packaging with a restricted embedded area; end-to-end execution is not evidenced.
execution_evidence: Public repo and live demo are reported.
About text describes local parsing and proof generation.
Devpost screenshot provides packaging only and does not show a running workflow.
impact_rationale: Patients and clinical decision-support systems have a high-stakes need to use genetic facts without exposing immutable DNA; the proposed solution directly addresses that risk.
impact_evidence: About text gives Plavix contraindication as a concrete clinical use case.
Privacy-preserving pattern generalizes to other sensitive datasets.
creativity_rationale: Pairing WebMCP with zero-knowledge proofs at the browser trust boundary is an unusually ambitious and memorable application.
creativity_evidence: Raw genome never enters the agent context by design.
The project frames proof of conclusion rather than disclosure of source data.
usability_note: The safety model is compelling, but clinical interpretation, setup, and proof latency are not shown.
red_flags: High-stakes medical and cryptographic claims are not execution-verified in the packet.
advance_reason: Potentially transformative and highly original, but should advance with explicit evidence caveat.

one_line: An agent-native SOC console for investigating login-abuse incidents through typed security tools.
what_it_does: Lets an agent search logs, investigate users, analyze IPs, score risk, map MITRE techniques, and produce incident reports from dashboard telemetry.
leverage_rationale: Typed tools eliminate fragile log scraping and make repeatable multi-step pivots across security telemetry practical; the agent is central to the investigation workflow.
leverage_evidence: About text contrasts DOM scraping/click scripting with named typed tools.
Six tools expose investigation operations such as investigate_user and risk scoring.
Frames show investigation/progress and evidence-oriented console screens.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent SOC workflow and product screens, but no video means the start-to-finish investigation is claimed rather than directly demonstrated.
execution_evidence: Three frame sheets show security product screens and investigative workflow.
About text defines a concrete login-abuse case from ranking through report.
Public repo and live demo are reported.
impact_rationale: Security analysts face repeated, high-volume pivoting across auth telemetry; consolidating evidence and report generation addresses a real operational burden.
impact_evidence: About text identifies Tier-2 analysts and tens of thousands of auth events.
Product scope includes evidence-backed findings and incident reports.
creativity_rationale: Agent-native SOC investigation is a strong, timely synthesis with a concrete workflow, though the security-console category is established.
creativity_evidence: Named typed pivots replace generic dashboard scraping.
The product combines ML scoring, threat intelligence, and agent investigation.
usability_note: The evidence-oriented console appears useful for analysts, but operational accuracy and false-positive handling are unverified.
red_flags: No submitted video; ML/security performance is not independently evidenced.
standouts: Strong rationale for typed tools over scraping.
advance_reason: Credible agent-native security workflow with meaningful reliability gains and clear audience need.

one_line: A browser workbench where agents and humans co-explore physical assemblies through typed topology operations.
what_it_does: Provides live assembly context, approved components, layout validation, bounded topology generation, load-case inspection, and human-only promotion decisions.
leverage_rationale: Agents receive exact live topology, protected volumes, and load-case state and can make bounded typed changes, avoiding stale screenshots and hidden engineering state.
leverage_evidence: About text lists typed operations over exact live design context.
Shared viewport reflects topology, stress/displacement fields, replay, and action receipts.
Human-only decision boundary prevents silent promotion.
execution_rationale: The product description is unusually careful and coherent, but the packet has no video and frame sheets are the only visual evidence, limiting end-to-end credit.
execution_evidence: Three frame sheets are submitted and show the design workbench/assembly workflow.
About text describes validation, topology candidates, and receipts.
Live demo is reported alive.
impact_rationale: Small drone and robotics teams have a credible need for earlier, more inspectable concept exploration before heavy engineering tools.
impact_evidence: About text names small drone and robotics teams and narrows the claim to early exploration.
The workflow exposes physical-design state for review.
creativity_rationale: Co-steering physical assemblies with visible topology evidence, replay, and bounded approvals is an ambitious interaction model beyond generic CAD chat.
creativity_evidence: Agent actions are reflected in the same viewport with receipts.
Topology generation and load cases are exposed as structured collaboration.
usability_note: The intended engineering audience is clear, but complexity and domain correctness are not demonstrated sufficiently.
red_flags: No video; engineering validity is expressly not a manufacturing or approval replacement.
advance_reason: Ambitious and credible early-stage physical-design collaboration concept, with evidence limits noted.

one_line: An AI film-production manager that turns scripts into weather-aware schedules, tasks, and call sheets.
what_it_does: Analyzes multilingual screenplays, extracts production elements, schedules scenes around weather, tracks departments, and exports call sheets through WebMCP tools.
leverage_rationale: Structured screenplay, schedule, weather, and department state makes coordination more reliable than chat advice, though a general agent could reproduce much of it with friction.
leverage_evidence: Pitch specifies eight WebMCP tools.
About text names analyze_script, get_weather_forecast, generate_schedule, assign_task, status, and export tools.
Frames show production-management screens.
execution_rationale: The scope is coherent and the packet shows a production dashboard, but no video or end-to-end call-sheet workflow is available.
execution_evidence: Three frame sheets show scheduling/task-management interface.
About text defines script-to-schedule-to-call-sheet flow.
Live demo is reported alive.
impact_rationale: Film producers coordinating many departments face real spreadsheet and weather-change overhead; the product addresses a concrete operational pain.
impact_evidence: About text identifies 10+ departments, paper call sheets, and weather-triggered replanning.
Features directly map to those coordination needs.
creativity_rationale: Weather-aware production planning and agent-operated department coordination are a fresh synthesis, though scheduling tools are familiar.
creativity_evidence: Arabic/English/French screenplay analysis is included.
Outdoor scenes can move indoors based on weather probability.
usability_note: The production workflow is recognizable, but multilingual parsing and schedule correctness are not observed.
red_flags: No submitted video; weather and schedule behavior are not directly verified.
standouts: Good mapping from script to operational artifacts.
advance_reason: Clear audience and credible coordination problem, with moderate WebMCP delta and evidence limits.

one_line: A live wedding seating canvas where people and agents arrange guests while preserving constraints and reversibility.
what_it_does: Manages guests, tables, venue rules, conflicts, agent proposals, minimal repairs, undo, and printable seating documents in a shared visual chart.
leverage_rationale: The agent reads and mutates shared seating, venue, and constraint state while reacting to human changes; this is substantially more reliable than a separate chat suggestion.
leverage_evidence: 170-second transcript shows agent loading guests, seating, adding a bar, detecting a broken rule, and repairing it.
About text says tools dynamically reflect chart state and finalize only when valid.
Video visibly includes agent cursor, activity log, and live chart changes.
execution_rationale: The video demonstrates a complete workflow from loading through seating, manual conflict, minimal repair, and printing, with clear UI state and activity history.
execution_evidence: Video is present and 170 seconds long with detailed transcript.
Transcript covers venue rules, guests/tables, agent seating, conflict detection, repair, and print section.
Frames show the seating canvas and sidebars.
impact_rationale: Couples and planners face a real combinatorial and interpersonal seating problem; the product supports both constraints and human judgment.
impact_evidence: About text identifies capacity, relationships, venue zones, pins, and family compromises.
Video demonstrates a broken rule being repaired with the smallest change.
creativity_rationale: The shared spatial artifact, relationship constraints, minimal-change repairs, and dynamic tool availability make a memorable human-agent planning model.
creativity_evidence: Agent reacts to a manual move instead of overwriting it.
Finalize tool appears only when the chart is valid.
usability_note: The visual canvas, logs, and reversible decisions make the workflow understandable; wedding-specific complexity remains.
advance_reason: Strongly demonstrated shared-state WebMCP collaboration with clear audience value and polished workflow.

one_line: An accessible-by-default browser editor exposing code, preview, audits, and design-system checks to agents.
what_it_does: Edits multi-file HTML/CSS/JS, previews responsively, runs WCAG audits, checks contrast and design tokens, and exposes the loop through WebMCP.
leverage_rationale: The agent can operate on the editor and inspect the same live preview and accessibility audit, closing the write-check loop more reliably than separate UI automation.
leverage_evidence: Pitch explicitly says the editor, preview, and WCAG audit are exposed via WebMCP.
About text describes agent-written code being checked in the same tab.
Frames show the browser editor/workflow and configuration panels.
execution_rationale: The described surface is coherent and visually packaged, but the supplied video is a misleading unrelated title and there is no reliable end-to-end demo transcript.
execution_evidence: About text specifies editor, preview, audit, responsive preview, and design-system checks.
Frame sheets show a visual editor/workflow interface.
FACTS report a live demo but video title is unrelated.
impact_rationale: Front-end teams and agents routinely miss accessibility and design-system regressions; integrated audits address a concrete quality problem.
impact_evidence: About text identifies accessibility leakage across editor/browser/checker handoffs.
Features include WCAG violations, exact elements, contrast, and token drift.
creativity_rationale: Combining agentic front-end editing with continuous a11y and design-system feedback is a useful fresh synthesis, though editors and audits are known categories.
creativity_evidence: A single tab closes code-preview-audit loop.
DESIGN.md token drift checks are integrated into editing.
usability_note: The one-tab workflow is promising, but the packet does not establish reliability of audits or preview behavior.
red_flags: Reported video title is Rick Astley rather than a product demo.
No public repo and no trustworthy video evidence.
standouts: Design-token and browser-compatibility checks extend beyond basic editing.
advance_reason: Good concept and stated WebMCP rationale, but the contradictory video metadata materially weakens execution and eligibility confidence.
